name: occurrence
title: Occurrence
description: A dwc:Event that establishes the state of a dwc:Organism at a particular place and time.
examples: `a wolf pack on the shore of Kluane Lake in 1988`; `a virus in a plant leaf in the New York Botanical Garden at 15:29 on 2014-10-23`; `a fungus in Central Park in the summer of 1929`

fields.name: occurrence_pk
fields.title: Occurrence (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:Occurrence.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.

fields.name: occurrenceID
fields.title: Occurrence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Occurrence.
fields.notes: The value in this field MUST be preserved in aggregation. Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: event_fk
fields.title: Event (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Event.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: isPartOfOccurrence_fk
fields.title: Is Part Of Occurrence (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Occurrence of which this dwc:Occurrence is a part.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: occurrenceProtocol_fk
fields.title: Occurrence Protocol (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Protocol used for a dwc:Occurrence.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: surveyTarget_fk
fields.title: Survey Target (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for an eco:SurveyTarget.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: recordNumber
fields.title: Record Number
fields.description: An identifier given to the dwc:Occurrence at the time it was recorded. Often serves as a link between field notes and a dwc:MaterialEntity record, such as a specimen collector's number.
fields.notes: Often serves as a link between field notes and a dwc:MaterialEntity, such as a specimen collector's number.

fields.name: organismQuantity
fields.title: Organism Quantity
fields.description: A number or enumeration value for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.notes: A dwc:organismQuantity must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantityType.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)

fields.name: organismQuantityType
fields.title: Organism Quantity Type
fields.description: The type of quantification system used for the quantity of dwc:Organisms.
fields.notes: A dwc:organismQuantityType must have a corresponding dwc:organismQuantity. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `27` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType); `12.5` (organismQuantity) with `% biomass` (organismQuantityType); `r` (organismQuantity) with `Braun-Blanquet Scale` (organismQuantityType); `many` (organismQuantity) with `individuals` (organismQuantityType)

fields.name: sex
fields.title: Sex
fields.description: A sex of a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: lifeStage
fields.title: Life Stage
fields.description: An age class or life stage of a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: reproductiveCondition
fields.title: Reproductive Condition
fields.description: A reproductive condition of a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: caste
fields.title: Caste
fields.description: A social caste of a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary that aligns best with a dwc:Taxon. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: behavior
fields.title: Behavior
fields.description: A behavior shown by a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: vitality
fields.title: Vitality
fields.description: An indication of whether a dwc:Organism was alive or dead at the time of collection or observation.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: establishmentMeans
fields.title: Establishment Means
fields.description: Statement about whether a dwc:Organism has been introduced to a given place and time through the direct or indirect activity of modern humans.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use controlled value strings from the controlled vocabulary designated for use with this term, listed at http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/doc/em/. For details, refer to https://doi.org/10.3897/biss.3.38084. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: degreeOfEstablishment
fields.title: Degree Of Establishment
fields.description: The degree to which a dwc:Organism survives, reproduces, and expands its range at the given place and time.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use controlled value strings from the controlled vocabulary designated for use with this term, listed at http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/doc/doe/. For details, refer to https://doi.org/10.3897/biss.3.38084. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: pathway
fields.title: Pathway
fields.description: The process by which a dwc:Organism came to be in a given place at a given time.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use controlled value strings from the controlled vocabulary designated for use with this term, listed at http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/doc/pw/. For details, refer to https://doi.org/10.3897/biss.3.38084. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: substrate
fields.title: Substrate
fields.description: A type of biotic or abiotic material to which a dwc:Organism was attached during a dwc:Occurrence.
fields.notes: No inference can be made from this term that a dwc:Organism interacted in any other way than being connected to some (not a particular) material resource of the substrate type (such as during parasitization or decomposition). A host-parasite relationship is better expressed as a dwc:OrganismInteraction. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: occurrenceStatus
fields.title: Occurrence Status
fields.description: A statement about the detection or non-detection of a dwc:Organism during a dwc:Event.
fields.notes: For dwc:Occurrences, the default vocabulary is recommended to consist of 'detected' and 'notDetected', but can be extended by implementers with good justification. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: occurrenceReferences
fields.title: Occurrence References
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers (publication, bibliographic reference, global unique identifier, URI) of literature associated with the dwc:Occurrence.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space ( | ). Note that the intended usage of the term dcterms:references in Darwin Core is to point to the definitive source representation of the resource, if one is available. Note also that the intended usage of dcterms:bibliographicCitation in Darwin Core is to provide the preferred way to cite the resource itself.
fields.examples: `http://www.sciencemag.org/cgi/content/abstract/322/5899/261`; `Christopher J. Conroy, Jennifer L. Neuwald. 2008. Phylogeographic study of the California vole, Microtus californicus Journal of Mammalogy, 89(3):755-767.`; `Steven R. Hoofer and Ronald A. Van Den Bussche. 2001. Phylogenetic Relationships of Plecotine Bats and Allies Based on Mitochondrial Ribosomal Sequences. Journal of Mammalogy 82(1):131-137. | Walker, Faith M., Jeffrey T. Foster, Kevin P. Drees, Carol L. Chambers. 2014. Spotted bat (Euderma maculatum) microsatellite discovery using illumina sequencing. Conservation Genetics Resources.`; `https://doi.org/10.3897/BDJ.14.e177525`

fields.name: occurrenceRemarks
fields.title: Occurrence Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Occurrence.

fields.name: organism_fk
fields.title: Organism (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: organismID
fields.title: Organism ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY refer to a dwc:Organism within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.

fields.name: organismScope
fields.title: Organism Scope
fields.description: A description of the kind of dwc:Organism instance. Can be used to indicate whether the dwc:Organism instance represents a discrete organism or if it represents a particular type of aggregation.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.

fields.name: organismName
fields.title: Organism Name
fields.description: A textual name or label assigned to a dwc:Organism instance.

fields.name: causeOfDeath
fields.title: Cause Of Death
fields.description: An indication of the known or suspected cause of death of a dwc:Organism.
fields.notes: The cause may be due to natural causes (e.g., disease, predation), human-related activities (e.g., roadkill, pollution), or other environmental factors (e.g., extreme weather events).

fields.name: organismRemarks
fields.title: Organism Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Organism instance.
fields.notes: `One of a litter of six`

fields.name: verbatimIdentification
fields.title: Verbatim Identification
fields.description: A string representing the classification as it appeared in the original record.
fields.notes: This term is meant to allow the capture of an unaltered original identification/determination, including identification qualifiers, hybrid formulas, uncertainties, etc. This term is meant to be used in addition to dwc:geologicalMaterialName or dwc:scientificName (and dwc:identificationQualifier etc.), not instead of it.
fields.examples: `Peromyscus sp.`; `Ministrymon sp. nov. 1`; `Anser anser × Branta canadensis`; `Pachyporidae?`, `Potentilla × pantotricha Soják`; `Aconitum pilipes × A. variegatum; `Lepomis auritus x cyanellus`

fields.name: identifiedBy
fields.title: Identified By
fields.description: A name for a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
fields.notes: When used in the context of a Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the Event. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).

fields.name: identifiedBy_fk
fields.title: Identified By (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: identifiedByID
fields.title: Identified By ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dcterms:Agent responsible for making a dwc:Identification.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY refer to a dcterms:Agent within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.
fields.examples: `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097` (for an individual); `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097 | https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0098` (for a list of people)

fields.name: dateIdentified
fields.title: Date Identified
fields.description: The date on which the subject was determined as representing the dwc:Taxon.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a date that conforms to ISO 8601-1:2019.
fields.examples: `1963-03-08T14:07-06:00` (8 Mar 1963 at or after 2:07pm and before 2:08pm in the time zone six hours earlier than UTC); `2009-02-20T08:40Z` (20 February 2009 at or after 8:40am and before 8:41 UTC); `2018-08-29T15:19` (29 August 2018 at or after 3:19pm and before 3:20pm local time); `1809-02-12` (within the day 12 February 1809); `1906-06` (in the month of June 1906); `1971` (in the year 1971); `2007-03-01T13:00:00Z/2008-05-11T15:30:00Z` (some time within the interval beginning 1 March 2007 at 1pm UTC and before 11 May 2008 at 3:30pm UTC); `1900/1909` (some time within the interval between the beginning of the year 1900 and before the year 1909); `2007-11-13/15` (some time in the interval between the beginning of 13 November 2007 and before 15 November 2007)

fields.name: identificationReferences
fields.title: Identification References
fields.description: A list (concatenated and separated) of dcterms:BibliographicResources used in a dwc:Identification.
fields.notes: When used in the context of a Survey, the subject consists of all of the dwc:Identifications related to the Survey. Recommended best practice is to separate the values in a list with space vertical bar space (` | `).
fields.examples: `Aves del Noroeste Patagonico. Christie et al. 2004.`; `Stebbins, R. Field Guide to Western Reptiles and Amphibians. 3rd Edition. 2003. | Irschick, D.J. and Shaffer, H.B. (1997). The polytypic species revisited: Morphological differentiation among tiger salamanders (Ambystoma tigrinum) (Amphibia: Caudata). Herpetologica, 53(1), 30-49.`

fields.name: identificationVerificationStatus
fields.title: Identification Verification Status
fields.description: A categorical indicator of the extent to which a taxonomic determination has been verified to be correct.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as that used in HISPID and ABCD.

fields.name: identificationRemarks
fields.title: Identification Remarks
fields.description: Comments or notes about the dwc:Identification.
fields.examples: `Distinguished between Anthus correndera and Anthus hellmayri based on the comparative lengths of the uñas.`

fields.name: taxonID
fields.title: Taxon ID
fields.description: An identifier for a dwc:Taxon.
fields.notes: In DwC-DP, the taxonID is always an external link to a taxon record. As such, if present, it should be a resolvable globally unique identifier. See the Identifiers section of https://github.com/CatalogueOfLife/coldp/blob/master/README.md.

fields.name: scientificNameID
fields.title: Scientific Name ID
fields.description: An identifier for the nomenclatural (not taxonomic) details of a scientific name.
fields.notes: In DwC-DP, the taxonID is always an external link to a taxon record. As such, if present, it should be a resolvable globally unique identifier. See the Identifiers section of https://github.com/CatalogueOfLife/coldp/blob/master/README.md.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.title: Scientific Name
fields.description: A scientific name string, not including authorship, date or identification qualifiers.
fields.examples: `Coleoptera` (order); `Vespertilionidae` (family); `Manis` (genus); `Ctenomys sociabilis` (genus + specificEpithet); `Ambystoma tigrinum diaboli` (genus + specificEpithet + infraspecificEpithet); `Quercus agrifolia var. oxyadenia` (genus + specificEpithet + taxonRank + infraspecificEpithet); `×Agropogon littoralis`; `Mentha ×smithiana`; `Agrostis stolonifera L. × Polypogon monspeliensis`

fields.name: scientificNameAuthorship
fields.title: Scientific Name Authorship
fields.description: The authorship information for a dwc:scientificName formatted according to the conventions of the applicable dwc:nomenclaturalCode.

fields.name: vernacularName
fields.title: Vernacular Name
fields.description: A common or vernacular name.

fields.name: taxonRank
fields.title: Taxon Rank
fields.description: A taxonomic rank of the most specific name in a dwc:scientificName.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. The taxon ranks of algae, fungi and plants are defined in the International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (Shenzhen Code Articles H3.2, H4.4 and H.3.1).

fields.name: classificationSystem
fields.title: Classification System
fields.description: A reference to the classification system in which an authoritative name or formal classification belongs.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to provide a formal citation or IRI. This term should not be confused with dwc:namePublishedIn as a classification system is not equivalent to a publication in which a taxon is first described. This term should not be confused with dwc:nameAccordingTo as a classification system is not equivalent to a publication or other source in which a specific taxon concept circumscription is defined or implied. This term should not be confused with dwc:nomenclaturalCode as a classification system is not equivalent to code of nomenclature, which states the rules for naming rather than an organized source of names. This term has an equivalent in the dwciri: namespace that allows only an IRI as a value, whereas this term allows for any string literal value.
fields.examples: `Strunz, H., Nickel, E.H. (2001): Strunz Mineralogical Tables. Chemical-Structural Mineral Classification System. 9th edition. E. Schweizerbart’sche Verlagsbuchhandlung, Stuttgart, ix + 870 p. (ISBN 3-510-65188-X)`; `Gaines, R.V., Skinner, H.C.W., Foord, E.E., Mason, B., Rosenzweig, A. (1997): Dana's New Mineralogy: The System of Mineralogy of James Dwight Dana and Edward Salisbury Dana. 8th edition. John Wiley & Sons, New York, xlv + 1819 p. (ISBN 0-471-19310-0).`; `https://kos.geospecimens.org/vocab/meteorite-classification`; `Mammal Diversity Database. (2026). Mammal Diversity Database (Version 2.5) [Data set]. [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/10595931). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17033774`; `Index Fungorum. (2026). Index Fungorum electronic database. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Retrieved August 17, 2026, from indexfungorum.org.`

fields.name: informationWithheld
fields.title: Information Withheld
fields.description: Additional information that exists about a resource, but that is not shared publicly. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
fields.examples: `location information not given for endangered species`; `collector identities withheld | ask about tissue samples`

fields.name: dataGeneralizations
fields.title: Data Generalizations
fields.description: Actions taken to make the shared data less specific or complete than in its original form. Suggests that alternative data of higher quality may be available on request.
fields.examples: `Coordinates generalized from original GPS coordinates to the nearest half degree grid cell.`

fields.name: feedbackURL
fields.title: Feedback URL
fields.description: A uniform resource locator (URL) that points to a webpage on which a form may be submitted to gather feedback about the record.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to optionally include query strings that act to pre-populate web page form elements and communicate the context.
